FILED s543m (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24), found by member 2's probes (#5374).  PRE-EXISTING: base 9fc6583b the same.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | ./runpcl; scratch/s543m/p2/f.pl line f9):
    { package Q9; our $w9 = 1; my $w9 = 4; print "f9 ", $w9 + 1, " $Q9::w9\n"; }
  perl  f9 5 1        PCL  f9 5 4

WHAT IT IS (suspect, not measured): a FILE-LEVEL bare block that opens with `package Q9;` is flattened into its own section (read in-package Q9), so the lexical `my $w9` is a `let` of the symbol `$w9` interned in Q9 -- and the qualified spelling `$Q9::w9` IS that symbol: the `let` shadows the package variable for every spelling of it (the my-shadow mechanism).  #470's rule (a file that spells the package variable qualified takes the mangle for the lexical) covers a PROMOTED file lexical; this one is an ordinary `let` in the section.  Also check `package Q9; my $v = 4; print $Q9::v` at the top level (no block) and `$main::x` beside a top-level `my $x` in main.

=== APPENDED s543m (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-27): the review's F7 -- #5374's residue, file level AND eval text, base 9a3ce86f = tree ===
The reviewing session's y-02 (`~/pcl-agent-scratch/s543/review/probes-1127/rm2/p/y-02.pl`, nine rows) widens this task: in ONE scope an `our` and then a `my` of the same name, then the QUALIFIED read:
    package P; our $y = "gy"; my $y = "ly"; print "$y $P::y\n";          # perl: ly gy    PCL: ly ly
    our @w = (1,2); my @w = (3); print "@w | @P::w\n";                    # perl: 3 | 1 2  PCL: 3 | 3
the same in a file-level block, in an eval text with and without `package` in the text (`eval q{ our $y = "gy"; my $y = "ly"; "$y $P::y" }`); s543m's om_* rows never read the qualified name after the `my` at the text's top level (om_block does, inside a sub, and is right).
IS IT THE IDENTITY CELL (#5352's family)?  NO -- measured (scratch/s543m/p11/f7.pl, `PCL_OPT=-line-track ./pl2cl`): the `my` is a `p-let` of the bare name read in the section's package, `(p-let (($y :scalar "ly")) ...)` under `(in-package P)`, so the let binds the symbol `P::$y`, and the qualified `$P::y` lowers to the SAME CL symbol `P::$y`: inside the let's scope it reads the lexical (a `let` of a symbol-macro name shadows it -- the my-shadow mechanism).  The array twin likewise: `my @w = (3)` is `(p-let ((@w :array ...)) (p-array-= P::@w (vector 3)) ...)` and both `@w` and `@P::w` read the let.  Direction: a qualified read whose package-variable symbol is shadowed by a lexical `let` of the same symbol must spell the package variable through its cell (`symbol-value` of the defcell / the global accessor), not the symbol; or the lexical gets a mangled name when a qualified spelling of the same symbol occurs in its scope (the identity-cell rule's own exception, ExprToCL `_own_name_cell_ok`).  Rare (perl warns about the masking).
ALSO (LOUD, base too): `our $z = 1; my $z = 2; our $z;` at file level is a transpile refusal `Parser2 TODO: our '$z' shadows a my-lexical`.
